correctness.rationale: For antiunitary A on C^2, the ordinary overlap modulus covers [0,c] by a quadratic polynomial zero, compactness, and connectedness. The q-pair constraint decomposes y into a fixed x component and a unit orthogonal component. The resulting two vector components have magnitudes rm and d sqrt(1-m^2); independent orthogonal phase gives an exact interval of moduli. The maxima and minima on 0<=m<=c give the two piecewise radii, and compact connected frame space plus rotation covariance fill the closed annulus. Endpoint cases and a realizing rotation-conjugation family are explicit. Supplementary rational and random tests agree; no finite experiment is used as the universal proof.

The full convexity classification and distinct sharp norm-attainment plateau are natural geometric invariants, with both phase thresholds realized throughout the one-parameter family of planar antiunitaries. The result is neither arbitrary parameter slicing nor a restatement of the ordinary q=1 disk.
